package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The article discusses general risks and best practices regarding software supply chain security, emphasizing the dangers of vulnerable or low-quality dependencies and the importance of DevOps automation for rapid vulnerability response.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected or unauthorized network requests during build or install phases
Automated dependency upgrades or removals outside of scheduled maintenance
Unusual access to sensitive files or environment variables by dependencies
file_indicators: References to untrusted or unknown external repositories in dependency files
Unexpected changes in lockfiles (package-lock.json, requirements.txt, etc.)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains not associated with official package registries
Connections to known malicious or suspicious IPs/domains during CI/CD
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously scan all dependencies for known vulnerabilities and license issues with every build. Monitor for unexpected network activity or file access during installation and runtime. Use local mirrors for dependencies to reduce risk of supply chain attacks. Automate reporting and alerting for any changes in dependency status or vulnerability disclosures. Integrate rapid patching and deployment processes to minimize exposure windows after vulnerability disclosures.
